actions.action: Inspect leaf undersides for spider mite webbing or speckles
Tip plant out of pot and check roots and corm
Cut away mushy roots and soft corm parts if present
Remove collapsed, yellow and dead leaves
Repot into chunky soil/orchid bark/perlite mix in a draining pot slightly larger than root ball at original depth
If metal pot has no holes, use it as a cover pot and empty standing water after watering
Check top 2 inches of soil for dryness before watering
Water thoroughly when top 2 inches are dry
Scrape white mold off soil surface

reason: The answer catches the light and drainage issues but blames overwatering and root rot when the plant was actually underwatered and root-bound; its repot, window and thorough-watering advice overlaps the fix but is framed around drying out, though soil checks keep it from being harmful.
